title: Implementation of Guidelines from Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying
what_it_is: Implementation of Guidelines from Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on bullying review
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about caning safeguards, cyberbullying reports, and the Online Safety Act 2025 threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education arising from the Comprehensive Action Review against Bullying (a) whether the reasons why caning remains a suitable and effective punishment for upper primary and older boys can be shared; and (b) how will the Ministry ensure that schools carry out caning with the necessary safeguards in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education arising from the Comprehensive Action Review against Bullying (a) whether schools will be empowered to lodge cyberbullying reports for or against students to the Online Safety Commission; and (b) how will schools deal with cyberbullying content amongst students that may not reach the definitional threshold of online harms in the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025.

sections.label: Questions on caning and bullying measures
sections.summary: Questions ask about caning research, reporting channels, AI fake images, outcomes frameworks, and support for victims.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) with regard to the standardised caning measures outlined in the Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying, whether the distinctions in its application, including (i) between boys and girls and (ii) its commencement only from upper primary levels, are based on established research; and (b) if so, whether the Ministry can share the basis for these distinctions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry has conducted or relied on any studies evaluating the effectiveness of caning in reducing repeated bullying behaviour; and (b) what considerations inform its continued use, in light of international research linking corporal punishment to increased aggression and adverse long-term outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry requires schools to report bullying cases to the Ministry; and (b) what are the available channels for escalation or seeking further assistance should parents feel that their child's school has not handled their report of bullying adequately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there has been an increasing incidence of students creating and circulating AI-generated fake obscene images of fellow students in schools and educational institutions; and (b) whether the Ministry provides guidance on how such cases should be handled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in view of the planned implementation of standardised disciplinary measures in managing student misconduct (a) what outcomes framework, baselines, and quantified impact measurements, such as incident rates, recurrence, and reporting rates, will be used to assess bullying; (b) what is the intended timeframe for tracking such data; and (c) how will student well-being be measured and validated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what support is provided to victims of bullying who require care beyond school counselling, including referral pathways for clinical intervention; and (b) how does the Ministry safeguard students with mental health conditions or Special Educational Needs from being targeted by bullies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: My response will also cover related oral and written Parliamentary Questions set down for today's and subsequent Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These span four key areas and nine measures, forming a comprehensive whole-of-society approach.

sections.label: Stakeholder engagement in review
sections.summary: The Review engaged over 2,000 stakeholders including researchers, counsellors, psychologists, school leaders, staff, parents and students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As part of the Review, we also engaged various stakeholders, including professionals, such as researchers, counsellors and psychologists, as well as school leaders, school staff, parents and students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We engaged or received feedback from over 2,000 stakeholders in total.

sections.label: Tiered disciplinary actions
sections.summary: Actions are tiered by severity, from reflection and detention to suspension or caning for egregious or repeated serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Actions are tiered based on severity – from reflection and detention to suspension or caning for egregious or repeated serious offences.

sections.label: School anti-bullying policies
sections.summary: All schools will develop an anti-bullying policy by the end of this year based on MOE's guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All schools will also develop an anti-bullying policy by the end of this year that is based on MOE's guidelines.

sections.label: Caning as last resort
sections.summary: Schools use caning as a disciplinary measure if all other measures are inadequate, given the gravity of the misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Our schools use caning as a disciplinary measure if all the other measures are inadequate, given the gravity of the misconduct.

sections.label: Caning for boys only
sections.summary: Caning is used only for boys and only for egregious violations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Caning is meted out for boys only and, as I said earlier, only for egregious violations.

sections.label: School online reporting platform
sections.summary: From 2027, every school will have an online reporting platform for students and parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From 2027, each school will have an online reporting platform available for students and parents.

sections.label: Online Safety Commission assistance
sections.summary: When the Online Safety Commission becomes operational by end of June 2026, victims of certain online harms can seek more timely assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When the Online Safety Commission (OSC) becomes operational by the end of next month, June 2026, victims of certain online harms, such as online harassment, doxxing and intimate image abuse, will be able to seek more timely assistance.

sections.label: Educative restorative consequences
sections.summary: The consequences are educative, restorative and focused on helping the student learn and behave appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The consequences are educative, restorative and focused on helping the student learn and behave appropriately.

sections.label: MOE funding for schools
sections.summary: MOE will provide needs-based funding for schools to hire additional manpower or services while managing teacher workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MOE will, therefore, provide funding for our schools, on a needs-basis, to hire additional manpower or services to provide support while managing teacher workload.

sections.label: MOE offence management system
sections.summary: MOE is developing an offence management system to support case investigation, documentation and monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For a start, MOE is developing an offence management system to support case investigation, documentation and monitoring.

sections.label: Bullying incidence baseline data
sections.summary: Bullying incidents over the last five years averaged three per 1,000 primary and eight per 1,000 secondary students yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of data on bullying incidence, as a baseline, bullying incidents in the last five years averaged three incidents per 1,000 in our primary school students and eight per 1,000 secondary school students per year.

sections.label: Parent requests for school changes
sections.summary: Parents wanting seating, class or school changes should work with schools, which may activate MOE for safety plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On his first question, if a parent feels strongly that the child needs to change seating, change class, change school, please work closely with our schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And if needed, they will activate MOE to look at the specific circumstances and see what immediate safety plans need to be put in place and what longer-term arrangements need to be made.

sections.label: Online reporting and performance index
sections.summary: From next year all schools should have online reporting platforms, and bringing numbers down requires upstream work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Not to mention that from next year, all schools should have online reporting platforms to supplement the face-to-face reporting to school leaders, peer support leaders, as well as teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As to whether or not bringing the numbers down should be a meaningful key performance index, obviously, it is something that we want to watch, but it requires not just a downstream intervention and measures, but a lot of the work has to be upstream.

sections.label: Consistency, fairness and discipline guidelines
sections.summary: Schools have clearer guidelines and benchmarks balancing consistency and fairness with discretion, keeping education as discipline's core goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, it is always that balance between consistency and fairness, that principle, versus providing discretion to ensure that discipline ultimately has education as its core goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, our schools have been given clearer guidelines, some benchmarks to look at for different kinds of offences.

sections.label: Enhanced CCE role playing
sections.summary: CCE was enhanced with role playing and realistic scenarios for perspective-taking, empathy, being an upstander and seeking help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We looked at that and we felt that there was merit in that suggestion by some parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, we have enhanced CCE so that there is role playing, there are more realistic scenarios and allow the children to take on different roles in order for them to do better perspective-taking and strengthen the sense of empathy, and allow them to not just experience the emotions, but also what it is to be an upstander, and what it is to seek help if you are playing the role of the victim.

sections.label: Home-school and community partnerships
sections.summary: Teachers stay in touch with students facing complex home challenges, making home-school and community agency partnerships important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member's other point about families who face complex challenges at home that may manifest in terms of the child's behaviour, whether it is parentified behaviour, whether it is permissive parenting, whether it is a negative influence in the community or in the neighbourhood – this is something which our teachers will be more in touch with our students on; that is why the home-school partnership is so important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And that is why our partnerships with Family Service Centres, with the Social Service Offices (SSOs) as well as mental health agencies in the community, are so important.

sections.label: Escalation through MOE reporting channels
sections.summary: Serious matters can be escalated to School Leaders, Cluster Superintendents and Zonal Directors through MOE reporting channels, while minor cases should be nipped in the bud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If there is a need to escalate the matter, then certainly the School Leader and beyond that, the Cluster Superintendent and Zonal Director – these are people with experience who can be called upon through the MOE reporting channels to look into the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the Member's other question about how to ensure that minor cases do not crowd out more serious cases, certainly, we want to make sure that we look at the serious cases whilst not allowing minor incidents to then fester and become the shoots of more serious incidents, because it is better to nip in the bud.

sections.label: Formal apologies through restorative practice
sections.summary: Some schools facilitate formal apologies as restorative practice, bringing students together to seek closure when they are ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: With regard to formal apologies, there are some schools which will facilitate, as part of restorative practice, an opportunity to bring the two children or two young people together, or more if the incident involves more people, to try to bring closure when they are ready, particularly the student who has been subject to the bullying or hurtful behaviour.

sections.label: Published bullying recommendations and report
sections.summary: The Ministry published recommendations on handling school bullying, but the fuller report and findings behind them were not found.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, on what the Ministry has published on this matter, we read of course the recommendations being made about how to handle school bullying, but I was not able to find the fuller report or the findings on which the recommendations were based.

sections.label: 2024 AI deepfake disciplinary action
sections.summary: In 2024, secondary school students who created AI-generated obscene deepfakes of female students were identified and dealt with firmly through Police investigation and school disciplinary action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One may recall an unfortunate incident in 2024, where some secondary school students created AI-generated deep fakes of female students, obscene nudes – they were identified and they were dealt with firmly, not just through Police investigation but also by school disciplinary action.

sections.label: Affirmative answer to question
sections.summary: The answer to the second question is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On his second question, the answer is yes.

sections.label: Tracking recidivism and learning from mistakes
sections.summary: Schools observe whether a child learns from mistakes during disciplinary and corrective steps, and will see how best to track longer-term recidivism rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They will have a sense of whether a child learns from his or her mistake after the disciplinary and corrective and educative steps are put in place, and observe the child for the duration of his or her time in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will see how best to track this on the longer term, to look at overall recidivism rates.

sections.label: School measures against retaliation
sections.summary: Schools use peer support leaders and staff arrangements to protect students who report incidents or stand up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On fear of retaliation, there are, therefore, a whole range of school measures from peer support leaders being brought in; in addition, of course, school arrangements by staff to look after students who stand up or who report incidents that happen to them.
